hints.content: The graph of $y=|x|$ can be transformed to get the graph of $y=|x-1|-4$.  [[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
Suppose $f(x)=|x|$ and $g(x)=|x-1|-4$.  

>$\begin{align}f(x)&=|x|\\\\
f(x-1)&=|x-1|\\\\
f(x-1)-4&=|x-1|-4
\end{align}$

Notice that what is on the right-hand side of the equal sign is $g(x)$.  Therefore, $g(x)=f(x-1)-4$.  

Since function $g$ can be built from function $f$, the graph of function $g$ is a transformation of the graph of function $f$.

hints.content:
- Replacing $x$ with $x-1$ shifts the graph of $y=|x|$ to the right by $1$ unit.

- Adding $-4$ to the function shifts the graph of $y=|x|$ down by $4$ units.

Therefore, *the graph of $y=|x-1|-4$ is obtained by shifting the graph of $y=|x|$ to the right by $\text{ }1$ unit and down by $\text{ }4$ units.*

**The graph that corresponds with this transformation is graph $C$:**
